title: Power of a power and the zero index

draft.title: Power of a power and the zero index
card: A power of a power is a power raised to another power. To simplify it, multiply the indices: (a^m)^n = a^(m×n).
Worked example: (2³)² = 2³ × 2³ = 2⁶. The indices 3 × 2 give 6. Adding them would give 5, which is wrong here.
Any non-zero number to the power 0 equals 1. So 7⁰ = 1 and (−4)⁰ = 1.
draft.remember: Power of a power: multiply the indices. Non-zero number to the power 0: 1.

a.q: What is (3²)⁴ written as a single power of 3?
a.why: Multiply the indices: 2 × 4 = 8, so the answer is 3⁸. Adding them gives 3⁶, which is the rule for multiplying powers with the same base, not a power of a power.
a.clue: Which operation joins the two indices?

b.why: 6⁰ = 1 and (2³)⁰ = 2⁰ = 1, so the total is 1 + 1 + 5 = 7. Reading a zero index as 0 would give 5, which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Each number to the power 0 is worth the same amount.

final.title: Power of a power and the zero index
card: A power of a power is a power raised to another power. To simplify it, multiply the indices: \((a^{m})^{n} = a^{m \times n}\).
Worked example: \((2^{3})^{2} = 2^{3} \times 2^{3} = 2^{6}\). The indices \(3 \times 2\) give 6. Adding them would give 5, which is wrong here.
Any non-zero number to the power 0 equals 1. So \(7^{0} = 1\) and \((-4)^{0} = 1\).
final.remember: Power of a power: multiply the indices. Non-zero number to the power 0: 1.

a.q: What is \((3^{2})^{4}\) written as a single power of 3?
a.why: Multiply the indices: \(2 \times 4 = 8\), so the answer is \(3^{8}\). Adding them gives \(3^{6}\), which is the rule for multiplying powers with the same base, not a power of a power.
a.clue: Which operation joins the two indices?

b.why: \(6^{0} = 1\) and \((2^{3})^{0} = 2^{0} = 1\), so the total is \(1 + 1 + 5 = 7\). Reading a zero index as 0 would give 5, which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Each number to the power 0 is worth the same amount.
